key_insight: Simulated electromagnetic swirl in liquid-metal electrodes transitions toward chaos through a Ruelle–Takens–Newhouse sequence, with an intermediate strange non-chaotic attractor regime.
engineering_relevance: The Lorentz-to-viscous force ratio Q_m offers a useful organizing parameter for anticipating oscillatory flow in liquid-metal battery electrodes at fixed aspect ratio.
method: Three-dimensional simulations of cylindrical electrodes with varied geometry and applied current.
Vertical magnetic-field sweep from 0.1 to 20 G.
Dynamical analysis using phase portraits, FFT spectra, the 0–1 chaos test, autocorrelation and correlation dimension.
evidence_signal: Across currents of 11.11–100 A and radii of 3–9 cm, simulations show a consistent transition sequence and Reynolds-number scaling Re ∼ Q_m^(2/3).
watch_item: The critical Q_m for oscillatory onset changes when electrode height varies, so a universal threshold across geometries is not established.
paper_title: Transition to turbulence in swirl created by a vertical magnetic field in liquid metal electrodes
